title: Large personal Amiga and DOS native-recovery/source-preservation discovery
summary: Personally screen 429 candidate URLs and add 15 projects, with eight explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 24 query routes, screened 429 unique URLs and reviewed 23 repositories. Add 15 source-recovery, source-preservation and game-runtime projects, with eight non-promotion decisions. All four requested platforms were searched; no new CPC or Atari ST candidate cleared this pass without duplication or architectural qualification. Broad CPC/application searches produced substantial unrelated noise that was not promoted. Native game logic is distinguished from emulator-backed products, standalone matching from original-byte splicing, and stale introductory text from newer source/build evidence. No upstream game, build, installer or firmware was executed. Research flags remain qualified; no claim that all added projects are complete.

sources.reason: Native JavaScript artillery systems backed by original executable addresses, FPU decoding and independent execution probes; offline Python x86 oracle is separate from browser gameplay.
Original author preserves 1996 DOS C source and implements its thirteen piece patterns, scoring and indexed graphics in JavaScript.
Original 1996-97 DOS card game source is retained alongside a JavaScript port of its gameplay and original PCX/font formats.

Structured routine-addressed C from handwritten x86, with typed original data layout, SDL3 backend and separate AmigaOS/Picasso96 backend. Inspected ball and paddle algorithms are native C rather than register-machine translation.

Live DAT/LVL/graphics/audio decoding and editable native JavaScript entity state machines. Derived DHTML Lemmings mechanics and binary-format investigation coexist; no claim of an original-engine byte-matching decompilation.

Reko annotations, binary-format research and original BLD-script interpreter feed a Godot C# recreation. Game-script interpretation is not x86 emulation; a separate Spice86 setup supplies analysis evidence.

Go/Ebiten translation from a matching C recovery, plus original Amiga picture/music decoding and source-ported 68000 music. Inspected event-clock and animation routines are structured Go, not an instruction dispatcher.

Recovered Aztec C/assembly and typed-data accounting, with semantic map module and proof ledgers. Newer docs describe a 32-bit SDL3 compatibility port while the root README still says no independent build exists.
Deterministic flight captures, runtime contracts and named assembly slices; inspected ECM slice demonstrates symbolic 68000 recovery rather than P-code alone.
Structured C city/combat/diplomacy and SDL UI reconstructed from CIV.EXE with address maps and differential tests. Unicorn is an offline oracle, not the runtime game engine.

Replayable Ghidra annotations for the 16-bit DAGGER.EXE launcher, with intended behavioral recovery of the 32-bit FALL.EXE engine. The inspected tree contains launcher annotations, not a complete rebuilt game.
Standalone recovered Pascal game modules, including movement, collision, rendering, keyboard and XMS/sample interfaces. Explicitly functional rather than byte-matching recovery.
Partial C recovery of UFO2P/TACP with deterministic per-function matching and relocation/whole-image checks. Actual source units are committed; a game-wide source-only rebuild is not complete.
Recovered Microsoft/Lattice C and a separately implemented Python game/animation interpreter. Current animvm body is implemented despite stale stage-one header comments.
Annotated overlay-loader and startup reconstruction from Borland runtime embedded in Stronghold, documenting FBOV records, relocation and caller stack repair.
Reconstructs a historic Andy Warhol image from a photograph, not the ProPaint application or game source. Outside requested game/application scope.

Current browser executes original Amiga and DOS player-physics code in Musashi/x86 WebAssembly. Valuable extracted formats and bounded probes, but game-specific CPU execution is not a native game-source recovery; retain architecture audit.
README explicitly calls this an original Pengo-style prototype. Amiga porting/hardware research does not establish reconstruction of a historical game.
README explicitly identifies masm2c-style lifting, guest CPU registers/flags and a flat memory runtime. Retain generated-machine-model audit rather than label SDL packaging a native high-level port.

PC and browser variants execute original ST code using Musashi/JavaScript 68000. Separate Falcon patch source is present and potentially relevant, but requires a focused patch audit; do not promote the complete product as a native decompilation.

Static x86-to-C lifting retains runtime CPU, dispatch and interpreter modules. Native hook features do not establish whole-game high-level reconstruction; keep game-specific emulation audit separate from richardpenman/civ1.
Inspected tree has only README declaration, without committed reconstruction implementation. Preserve lead until actual source appears.

Tree contains an emu68-based music engine and bundled playback sources; not established as reconstruction of a requested historical game/application. Root README could not be decoded via blob fetch, so no stronger claim is made.
